title: Microsoft 365 admin center: set up Brand Center without enabling Public CDN
summary: The setup choice, permissions, licensing and tenant CDN command are supported by Microsoft documentation. The briefing correctly reports that Learn documents the choice while the roadmap still lists it as In development with an October 2026 target. The embedded instruction to report both sources was treated as page content, not as verification guidance.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to let administrators set up Brand Center without enabling Public CDN.
claims.quote: We are updating the Brand Center setup experience so that administrators can set up Brand Center without enabling Public CDN.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes Public CDN as previously enabled during setup even for branding governance capabilities that do not need it.
claims.quote: Today, Public CDN is enabled as part of Brand Center setup, even when an organization only wants to use branding governance capabilities that do not require it.

claims.claim: The planned change allows organisations to defer Public CDN until they need dependent capabilities such as organisational fonts.
claims.quote: With this update, organizations can begin using Brand Center while deferring Public CDN until they need capabilities that depend on it, such as organizational fonts.

claims.quote:
Scenario 1: Your tenant doesn't currently use the SharePoint organization assets feature.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: For tenants without organisation assets or using a private CDN, Public CDN (optional) is turned off by default at setup.
claims.quote: Under Public CDN (optional), choose whether to enable the public CDN now. Enable Public CDN (optional) if you plan to use brand fonts. The option is turned off by default.

claims.claim: For tenants already using organisation assets with a public CDN, Public CDN is already enabled and no additional CDN action is required.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Brand Center requires administrator setup before use, supporting admin-opt-in for this setup capability.
claims.quote: To enable the brand center, a Global Administrator completes a few steps in the Microsoft 365 admin center to create or activate the brand center app.

claims.claim: The setup option is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Brand center > Public CDN (optional).
claims.quote:
In the admin center, go to Settings > Org settings.
2. Select Brand center.
3. Enter a name for the brand center site, such as Brand Guide.
4. Under Public CDN (optional), choose whether to enable the public CDN now.

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenantCdnEnabled -CdnType Public -Enable $true enables the tenant's Public CDN using Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell.
claims.quote:
Module: Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell Module
Enables or disables Public content delivery network (CDN) or Private CDN on the tenant level.
Set-SPOTenantCdnEnabled -CdnType public -Enable $true

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Public CDN hosts brand fonts publicly, and publishing font files creates publicly stored catalog files alongside them.
claims.quote: By using this feature and publishing font files, a font catalog is created. The newly created font catalog files are publicly stored, along with the fonts, in the cloud

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Anyone with the font catalog file URLs, including people outside the organisation, can access the files.
claims.quote: The files are accessible to anyone, even people outside of your organization, who can get the URLs that link to them.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises against using the font feature for fonts containing proprietary information.
claims.quote: Don't use this feature if your fonts contain proprietary information

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft warns against using fonts with licence usage restrictions such as cloud-hosting restrictions.
claims.quote: Don't use this feature if your fonts contain proprietary information, or if they have license usage restrictions, such as restrictions on cloud hosting

claims.claim: Microsoft advises against using the font feature if the organisation is uncomfortable making its fonts publicly available.
claims.quote: or your organization isn't comfortable making the fonts publicly available.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Brand Center overview names no licence specific to Brand Center or its optional Public CDN setup choice.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint brand center licensing license requirements optional Public CDN. Read brand-center-overview in full and SharePoint service description licensing passages; the overview's licence statement concerns E3/E5 PowerPoint font support, not a separate Brand Center entitlement.

claims.claim: The Office 365 CDN service is included as part of a SharePoint Online subscription.
claims.quote: The Office 365 CDN service is included as part of your SharePoint Online subscription.

claims.claim: The Brand Center overview discusses Public CDN hosting and enablement rather than publishing its cost.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint brand center licensing license requirements optional Public CDN. Read brand-center-overview in full, CDN Quickstart and the CDN subscription passage; the overview gives no CDN price, while the CDN pages state subscription inclusion.

claims.claim: Learn does not state that the Brand Center setup choice calls Set-SPOTenantCdnEnabled.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint brand center enable Public CDN after setup settings Set-SPOTenantCdnEnabled. Read brand-center-overview, Set-SPOTenantCdnEnabled, CDN Quickstart and CDN command passages; they describe the choice and tenant command but not that implementation relationship.

claims.claim: The Brand Center overview gives no more detailed later-enablement path than brand center settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint brand center enable Public CDN after setup settings Set-SPOTenantCdnEnabled. Read brand-center-overview in full and the returned setup excerpts; later enablement is described only as from brand center settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a setup choice, not an agent, an automated action or a required action for tenants that already set up Brand Center.
claims.quote: We are updating the Brand Center setup experience so that administrators can set up Brand Center without enabling Public CDN.
